text: Setting clear project goals is essential for any successful team. A useful method is to create SMART goals, which means they are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying “improve the website,” you might set a goal to “increase page speed by 20% within three months.” To track progress, break the project into smaller milestones, such as completing the design phase or finishing the initial testing. Each milestone should have clear deliverables, or tangible results, like a report or a working prototype. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment by discussing these goals with everyone involved early on. When all parties agree on the objectives and timeline, the team can work together more smoothly and avoid misunderstandings.
